guideTitle: The Best CPU Stands Under $40, From Basic Dollies to Fan-Cooled Stands
metaTitle: Best CPU Stands Under $40: Rolling, Cooled and Charging Stands (2026)
metaDescription: We compared CPU stands under $40 on size range, load rating, casters and extras such as cooling fans, a wood finish and a charging station.
introParagraphs: Under $40 you can get more than a basic dolly. The stands here range from a $14 rolling base to options with a stated 110 lb rating, built-in cooling fans, a walnut-look finish and a two-tier stand with a charging station.

Start with fit: compare your case's width with the stand's range. Then decide whether an extra is worth paying for. Fans help only if your case draws air from the bottom; a charging tier helps if your desk is short of outlets.
Our comparison is based on published specifications and price position, not hands-on testing.

best-cpu-stands-under-40-1.summary: A YOSE stand at about $14, with almost no listed specifications.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-1.description:
The YOSE is the cheapest stand here, but its listing gives almost no specifications: no size range, capacity or caster details.

It is a reasonable gamble for a standard tower if you can confirm fit from the photos; otherwise the Hovadova or suptek list more.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-1.bestFor: Standard towers where fit can be checked from photos.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-1.skipIf: You want stated dimensions or capacity.

best-cpu-stands-under-40-2.summary: A Hovadova stand with four 360° locking casters and tool-free setup.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-2.description:
This Hovadova stand is the budget pick with locking casters, which keep the PC in place once positioned, and tool-free setup, for about $17 at the time of writing.

The listing does not state a size range or capacity.
cons: Size range and capacity not stated
best-cpu-stands-under-40-2.bestFor: Standard towers that should stay put.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-2.skipIf: You need a stated load rating; the suptek lists 110 lb.

best-cpu-stands-under-40-3.summary: A suptek rolling stand rated for 110 lb with a hollow, ventilated design.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-3.description:
The suptek is the stand with a stated load rating: 110 lb, with a hollow design for airflow and casters, for about $25 at the time of writing.

The listing gives conflicting width figures (7.8 to 14 inches in one place, 5.5 to 9.8 inches in another), so confirm the range for your case.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-3.skipIf: You want a clear width range; check with the seller first.

best-cpu-stands-under-40-4.summary: A walnut-look wood and PVC stand with a perforated platform.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-4.description:
The fulkun is the choice if the stand will be seen: wood pieces with PVC in a walnut look, with a perforated top for ventilation and casters.

It costs about $29 at the time of writing. The listing does not state size range or capacity.
specs: Material: wood and PVC, walnut look
cons: Size range and capacity not stated

best-cpu-stands-under-40-5.summary: A Hovadova stand with two built-in fans, adjustable from 9.05 to 12.59 inches wide.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-5.description:
The fan-equipped Hovadova adds two fans under the tower to move air beneath it, and adjusts from 9.05 to 12.59 inches wide, which suits wider cases.

It costs about $33 at the time of writing. Fans help most with cases that draw air from the bottom, and they need power.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-5.skipIf: Your case has no bottom intake; a plain stand is enough.

best-cpu-stands-under-40-6.summary: A ZIIWIND two-tier stand adjustable from 19.7 to 31.5 inches with a charging station.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-6.description:
The ZIIWIND is a two-tier stand, 16.9 x 11.4 inches with height adjustable from 19.7 to 31.5 inches, that holds the tower and adds a charging station for other devices.

It can sit under or beside the desk and costs about $40 at the time of writing.

The listing does not state capacity or the charging station's outputs.
cons: Charging outputs and capacity not stated
best-cpu-stands-under-40-6.bestFor: Desks short of outlets or storage.
best-cpu-stands-under-40-6.skipIf: You only need to lift the tower; a $15 stand does.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Compare your case width with the stand's range; the fan Hovadova lists 9.05–12.59 inches.
Only the suptek states one (110 lb).
Fans, a wood finish or a charging tier add cost; choose them only if they solve a problem.
Locking casters keep the PC in place.

faq.q: Do cooling fans in a stand help?
faq.a: They add airflow under the case, which helps most if your case draws air from the bottom.

faq.q: How much weight can these hold?
faq.a: Only the suptek states a capacity (110 lb). Check with the seller for the others.

faq.q: Is a two-tier stand worth it?
faq.a: If your desk lacks storage or outlets, yes. Otherwise a simple stand is enough.

bottomLine: For a heavier tower, the suptek is the pick with a stated 110 lb rating, once you confirm its width. The Hovadova with fans suits gaming towers with bottom intakes, and the fulkun suits visible setups.
The ZIIWIND adds storage and charging, and the YOSE and basic Hovadova are the budget options for standard towers.
